To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the annual cycle of extreme precipitation in The Netherlands is characterized by the North Atlantic Oscillation and that this cycle is different in different regions.
the annual cycle of extreme precipitation in The Netherlands is well represented by the GEV distribution with harmonic functions as location (mu) and scale (beta) parameters.
the annual cycle of daily extreme precipitation is non-stationary in the Netherlands and is influenced by the NAO.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of extreme events in the Netherlands and the attribution of the observed spatial and temporal patterns to the NAO.
the characterization of extreme precipitation in The Netherlands, and the identification of the factors responsible for its seasonal variability.
the seasonal variability of extreme rainfall in the Netherlands and its dependence on the NAO index.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the annual cycle of extreme precipitation in The Netherlands is influenced by both the NAO and the orography of the country, and that the annual cycle has a significant impact on the return period of extreme events.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to identify the seasonal variation of extreme precipitation events across the Netherlands, and we attributed it to the NAO index.
the non-stationarity of the GEV model is an important factor in representing the annual cycle of extreme precipitation in a spatially heterogeneous country like the Netherlands.
the non-stationarity of extreme precipitation in The Netherlands is significant and the seasonal variation of the extreme precipitation events is mainly driven by the NAO index.
The main takeaway from our work is that
non-stationary GEV models are more suitable for the analysis of extreme precipitation in The Netherlands than stationary GEV models.
the GEV model with non-stationary parameters is a useful tool for estimating extreme precipitation and for assessing the spatial and temporal variability of daily precipitation in the Netherlands.
the GEV parameters of extreme rainfall events are non-stationary and vary seasonally, and the NAO is the most influential climate factor in explaining the variation.
